habitat: Well-wooded country, especially mopane. It roosts by day under bushes and feeds at night in the open and on roads.
summary: An uncommon visitor and resident. Larger than most coursers, with red legs, a red eye-ring, a dark mask, and white eyebrows, throat and underparts. The upper parts and upper breast are light brown. The outer wing has a narrow iridescent purple trailing edge, hard to see. At night it calls ji-ku-it or a plaintive gro-raag. The immature’s head markings are less clear. Newman calls it both a visitor and a resident, so status and months were left unset. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Three-banded Courser has a chestnut V on the throat and two breast bands, with yellow legs. Bronze-winged Courser has red legs, a dark mask and white underparts.

head.pattern: Dark mask. White eyebrows and throat.

underparts.pattern: Light brown upper breast. Rest of the underparts white.

wings.pattern: Narrow iridescent purple trailing edge to the outer wing.

head.pattern: Head markings less clearly defined than the adult.

calls.description: At night, a shrill ji-ku-it or a plaintive gro-raag. Newman says coursers are not particularly vocal. Grade A call from Pafuri, Kruger. The filename names Bronze-winged Courser.
